pairs.subject: talking-avatar
pairs.evidence: apps/stage/src/voice/frame.ts:64 An utterance whose optional viseme list fails its checks (for example an unknown shape) is refused whole: session.ts reports it as a bad frame and never hands it to the player, so the sentence's PCM is never played, where the face timeline should have been dropped and the audio kept.

techniques.evidence: apps/stage/src/voice/frame.ts:64 The technique says a timeline that fails its checks is dropped and the sentence still plays. Here a bad timeline drops the audio too, and frame.test.ts pins this ('an unknown viseme' -> refused). The earlier verdict's anchor (line 60) was off by four lines.

apps/stage/src/voice/player.ts:4 One producer sits on the AudioContext heard clock. Speaking lasts while the heard time is inside a queued buffer, not until a pipeline event. emit() dedupes the signal, a new subscriber gets the last signal (player.ts:236), and session and player are lazy-imported (useVoice.ts:3).

apps/stage/src/voice/player.ts:39 The shape is looked up at the heard time (output latency removed) plus a lead of about one frame, on the consumer side. A voice with no visemes says 'the mouth follows loudness' in its status (session.ts:192).

pairs.registryProposal: per-sentence-face-sidecar states 'a timeline that fails its checks is dropped and the sentence still plays' for the voice/sidecar side only. When the mouth timeline rides inside the same wire frame as the audio, the consumer's frame validator is the usual place this leaks, so viseme-drive or face-signal-across-surfaces should name it: validate the face fields separately from the audio fields, and on failure strip the timeline, count it, and play the audio.

pairs.evidence: tools/rig/shadowrunr_rig/split.py:178 The offline splitter lifts a hand-authored region spec front to back with fills behind each part, decomposes the glow art as additive light deltas (the light-on-black variant), grounds what a solid always covers so no ghost copy stays behind, and runs as a reproducible command with a report and an extremes review.

techniques.evidence: tools/rig/shadowrunr_rig/split.py:178 Luminous parts are clamped additive deltas over the fill. Solids carry soft coverage, and an 'uncover'/covered mask grounds the hidden pixels (split.py:214-217). The README has extremes.png review and promote refuses a regression.

tools/avatar/learned_depth.py:17 Licences are audited per component: only the Apache-2.0 Small depth model is used, pinned by sha256 and user-installed rather than bundled. LaMa is also operator-installed (README:12).

tools/rig/README.md:97 The speaking element (the mouth light) is drawn procedurally by the renderer, not taken from generated mouth frames. The jaw is a hinged cut with a painted interior and an uncover strip.
tools/avatar/learned_depth.py:2 The only learned model here estimates depth, not motion.
tools/avatar/depth_map.py:2 These are offline prep tools, where pacing is irrelevant.
tools/rig/README.md:1 No per-sentence runtime process lives in this context.
